battle.name: 西班牙內戰
battle.theater: 伊比利亞半島與馬德里防線
battle.brief: 一九三六年七月十七日西班牙內戰爆發，國民軍與人民陣線政府全面開火，德義組織干涉、蘇聯輸送軍火。卡面這輛T-26輕型坦克是共和軍唯一成建制的裝甲力量，自巴塞羅那集結後投入馬德里防線、阿拉貢攻勢與埃布羅河決戰，以輕裝甲與直瞄火砲為步兵提供機動火力支撐。

kit.name: T-26輕型坦克
kit.history: 作為共和軍的主力輕型坦克，T-26在西班牙內戰中於城市防守與機動支援中提供裝甲火力。

countries: 交戰一方是西班牙第二共和國的人民陣線政府：一九三六年二月大選後由社會黨、共產黨與左翼自由派組成的聯盟執政，首都馬德里的國防委員會掌握軍權，總參謀長西希斯蒙多·卡薩多主持陸軍指揮部，陸軍與海軍多數單位效忠共和國，而CNT與UGT旗下的人民民兵團在數日內集結了數十萬武裝，補上了正規軍兵力不足的缺口；摩洛哥的土著軍團與駐紮的西班牙外來義勇軍在南部起義得手後被國民軍收編。另一方是國民軍：由莫拉、卡瓦涅亞斯與桑胡爾霍等人在摩洛哥、薩拉戈薩與馬德里分別策劃並指揮起義，北方另設布爾戈斯軍事委員會，卡爾派民兵在巴斯克與阿拉瓦一帶自行作戰；長槍黨與各地民兵團被整編進國民軍體系。外國支援方面，德國派出康多爾空軍團（航空兵、砲兵、突擊隊與工兵，鼎盛時約一萬九千人）與義大利的志願兵軍團（配屬數百架飛機）站在國民軍一側；蘇聯向共和國交付T-26坦克、飛機與火砲並派駐軍事顧問團，另有共產黨直接組建的國際縱隊（先後十九個縱隊，總兵力三萬五千至四萬五千人）參戰，墨西哥政府則提供物資與流亡者安置。蘇聯的援助以軍火為主，先後交付數百架飛機、千餘門火砲、數萬支步槍與上萬挺機槍，並有軍事顧問團常駐馬德里；共和國一方的另一支柱是墨西哥提供的資金與石油。英國與法國表面上主持不干預，實際上對共和國的武器封鎖同對國民軍的放行，暴露了歐洲大國對西班牙的計算。戰場同時延伸到海上：共和國海軍與軸心國潛艇在直布羅陀及地中海的較量，都令航運與補給成為戰局的一部分。
countriesEn: One side of the conflict was the Popular Front government of the Spanish Second Republic: after the February 1936 election a coalition of socialists, communists and left-leaning liberals took office, the National Defence Council in Madrid held the reins of military power, and the general staff under chief of staff Segismundo Casado directed the army, most of whose units and most of the navy stayed loyal to the Republic, while the worker militias of the CNT and the UGT rallied tens of thousands of armed men within days and filled the gap left by the understrength regular army; the Moroccan native regiments and the Spanish Foreign Legion stationed there went over to the insurgents in the south and were absorbed by the Nationalist army. The other side was the Nationalist army: the rising was planned and directed separately in Morocco, Zaragoza and Madrid by Mola, Cabanellas and Sanjurjo, a separate war council at Burgos directed the northern sector, and Carlist militias fought on their own account in the Basque country and in Álava; the Falange and the local militias were folded into the Nationalist structure. On foreign support, Germany sent the Condor Legion — air force, artillery, assault and engineer units, at its peak about nineteen thousand men — and Italy sent the Volunteer Corps with several hundred aircraft, both on the Nationalist side; the Soviet Union supplied the Republic with T-26 tanks, aircraft and artillery and posted military advisers, the communist International Brigades were raised directly and fought in the war (nineteen brigades in all, with a total strength of roughly thirty-five to forty-five thousand men), and the Mexican government provided material help and a place of refuge for exiles. Soviet aid came mainly in the form of matériel: several hundred aircraft, more than a thousand guns, tens of thousands of rifles and over ten thousand machine guns were delivered, and a mission of military advisers was stationed in Madrid, while Mexican money and oil were the Republic's other pillar. Britain and France claimed to run a non-intervention policy, yet the arms blockade they imposed on the Republic and the latitude they allowed the Nationalists exposed the arithmetic of the European powers over Spain. The war reached out to sea as well, with the Republican navy and Axis submarines contesting the Strait of Gibraltar and the Mediterranean, so that shipping and supply were part of the battle.
people: 關鍵人物橫跨兩條戰線。國民軍方面，策劃起義的桑胡爾霍在事成前一天由里斯本起飛時墜機身亡，接棒的是莫拉與卡瓦涅亞斯：卡瓦涅亞斯在馬德里起義後出任國民軍最高委員會主席，莫拉以「主任」身分主持北部與中部戰線，一九三七年六月三日飛機失事身亡；真正把各方捏成一個整體的是弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥，他在一九三六年十月被任命為國民軍總司令，一九三七年合併各方勢力，一九三八年自任「元帥」並統一政黨，最終宣布勝利。共和國方面，總理拉爾戈·卡瓦列羅是七月十九日後唯一有權組閣的人，他主張把鬥爭壓縮在防守馬德里，卻在民兵推動下發動了七月底由馬德里向托萊多推進的人民縱隊；繼任的普列托在一九三七年掌權，因反對犧牲加泰隆尼亞而於一九三八年辭職；共產黨人內格林掌握外交與供應，並在戰局不利時仍力主總攻；國防委員會主席何塞·米哈在馬德里扛住包圍與轟炸，參謀長卡薩多於一九三九年三月在拉斯特塞斯與佛朗哥的代表簽訂和約，隨即被解職。作戰層面最關鍵的是被士兵稱為「軍師」的恩里克·利斯特，他整編混成縱隊並以嚴格紀律統一國際縱隊；國際縱隊的「克萊伯」由曼弗雷德·斯特恩指揮。外軍方面，德國康多爾空軍團參謀長漢斯·馮·里希霍芬推動對地攻擊與傘兵工兵支援，義大利志願兵軍團團長埃托雷·安布羅西尼在埃布羅河戰役中陣亡；海明威、奧威等作家先後以戰地記者身分到前線，共產黨總書記伊巴魯里與巴斯克總統阿吉雷則是政治面最吃重的人物。西班牙以外的支援者亦有代表人物：美國的民眾救援組織與國際縱隊的後方服務處為志願者配備裝備與通行文件，加拿大與英國的志願者另組分隊，華盛頓的「西班牙民主委員會」則推動美國的對西班牙禁運；蘇聯派駐的軍事顧問負責砲兵與裝甲的技術指導。
peopleEn: The decisive figures stretch across both fronts. On the Nationalist side Sanjurjo, who had planned the rising, was killed in a plane crash on take-off from Lisbon on the eve of its success, and Mola and Cabanellas took over: Cabanellas became president of the Nationalist supreme council after the Madrid rising, Mola ran the northern and central fronts as the so-called Director and was killed in an aircraft accident on 3 June 1937, and the man who actually welded the various movements into one army was Francisco Franco, appointed commander-in-chief in October 1936, who merged the competing groups in 1937 and in 1938 took the title of Caudillo and unified the parties, and who would finally announce the victory. On the Republican side, Prime Minister Largo Caballero was the only man able to form a government after 19 July; he wanted to limit the struggle to the defence of Madrid, yet under pressure from the militias he launched the popular columns marching from Madrid towards Toledo in the last days of July. His successor Prieto took power in 1937 and resigned in 1938 because he opposed sacrificing Catalonia; the communist Negrín controlled foreign affairs and supply and pressed for a general offensive even when the situation was going against the Republic; José Miaja, president of the defence council, bore the siege and the bombing of Madrid, and the chief of staff Casado signed the surrender at Yeste in March 1939, only to be dismissed at once. At the operational level the most important figure was Enrique Líster, called the Guru by the troops, who reorganised the mixed brigades and imposed discipline on the International Brigades; the International Brigades were commanded by Manfred Stern under the name Kléber. Among the foreign contingents, Hans von Richthofen, chief of staff of the Condor Legion, drove close air support and the use of parachute and engineer troops, and Ettore Ambrosini, commander of the Italian Volunteer Corps, was killed in action at the Ebro; Hemingway, Orwell and other writers arrived as war correspondents, while Dolores Ibárruri of the communist party and the Basque president José Antonio Aguirre were the heaviest political names on the Republican side. The supporters outside Spain had faces of their own: American relief organisations and the International Brigades' rear services equipped volunteers and issued them papers, volunteers from Canada and Britain formed their own columns, and the Spanish Democratic Committee in Washington pressed for the American arms embargo, while Soviet military advisers directed the technical handling of the artillery and the armour.
kits: T-26是這場戰爭中共和軍唯一成建制的裝甲力量，也是卡面上這件武器的全部舞臺。它是一九三一年起在蘇聯生產的BT系衍生型輕型戰車，車重約五點六噸，乘員三人，裝甲厚度四十毫米以內，主砲為由二七式四十五公厘反戰車砲改裝的四十五公厘二十-K戰車砲，輔以同軸七點六二毫米機槍與車首機槍，公路极速約四公里。共和軍把它編為坦克營，每營十至二十輛，坦克連三至五輛，隸屬輕型坦克旅，最盛時共和軍有六個坦克旅，一九三七年合編為裝甲師，每師配T-26約百輛上下；國際縱隊第三十五縱隊下屬的阿斯圖里亞斯坦克營是外籍部隊中唯一成建制的裝甲營。由於馬力小、履帶與行走裝置脆弱，發動機在高溫下常熄火，車組多為臨時徵召且缺乏裝甲訓練，完好率長期偏低。國民軍一側的裝甲極少，早期只有少量繳獲的雷諾FT與民用裝甲汽車，一九三七年後義大利運來數十輛M11/39與M13/40中型坦克，另有少量繳獲的T-26被改編使用；其反裝甲骨幹是大批八十八毫米高射砲改作直瞄反戰車，加上七十五與一百零五毫米野砲、義大利七十/三十五步兵砲，以及由海軍重砲改裝的「提爾皮茨」號裝甲火車。空軍方面，共和國得到蘇聯的I-15雙座戰鬥機、I-16「哈托」單座戰鬥機與SB-2轟炸機；國民軍除義大利的Macchi與Savoia外，還有德國的He 111與Ju 52/3m，雙方飛機總數以數百架計。共和軍的城市防衛特別依賴街壘與反戰車砲：巴塞羅那與馬德里的工人武裝以路障把坦克同砲兵分隔開，時間一久，裝甲車的直射優勢便被房屋同瓦礫抵銷；而一旦裝甲車在街壘前停住，就會成為步兵反戰車武器的目標。
kitsEn: The T-26 was the only armoured force formed in the Spanish Civil War and the whole stage on which the vehicle shown on the card performed. It was a BT-derived light tank produced in the Soviet Union from 1931, weighing roughly 5.6 tonnes with a crew of three, protected by armour of less than forty millimetres and armed with the 45 mm 20-K gun converted from the 27M anti-tank gun, supported by a coaxial 7.62 mm machine gun and a hull machine gun, with a road speed of about four kilometres per hour. The Republican army organised it into tank battalions of ten to twenty vehicles, companies of three to five, subordinate to light tank brigades; at its peak the Republic fielded six tank brigades, and in 1937 these were combined into armoured divisions holding on the order of a hundred T-26s each; the Asturias tank battalion of the Thirty-Fifth International Brigade was the only formed armoured unit in the foreign volunteer forces. With so little power, with fragile tracks and running gear, with engines that overheated and stalled, and with crews hastily conscripted and untrained in armoured work, the operational rate of the fleet stayed low. On the Nationalist side armour was scarce: a handful of captured Renault FTs and civil armoured cars at first, then a few dozen Italian M11/39 and M13/40 medium tanks from 1937, plus a few captured T-26s put back into service; the backbone of Nationalist anti-tank defence was the mass of 88 mm flak guns turned into direct-fire anti-tank weapons, supported by 75 and 105 mm field guns and the Italian 70/35 infantry gun, and by the armoured train Tirpitz, rebuilt around naval heavy guns. In the air the Republic received Soviet I-15 two-seat fighters, I-16 Chato single-seat fighters and SB-2 bombers, while the Nationalists had Italian Macchi and Savoia machines alongside German He 111s and Ju 52/3m, both sides counting their aircraft in the hundreds. Urban defence in the Republic leaned heavily on street barricades and anti-tank guns: the workers' militias in Barcelona and Madrid used obstacles to separate armour from artillery, and once time was gained the advantage of direct fire faded against houses and rubble, while a tank halted at a barricade became a target for the anti-tank weapons of the infantry.
tactics: 共和軍的戰術核心，是把T-26當成可以移動的火砲，而不是突破用的主力：以營為單位分散到步兵縱隊前方數百公尺，進攻發起時以連為單位躍進，遭遇反戰車砲火便停進掩體等待步兵壓制，或退回掩體讓步兵先行；防守時採取縱深配置，坦克停在街口與建築物轉角充當射擊點，遇到敵方戰車則集中砲火打擊車體前部或履帶。進攻失利時的標準動作是退守與重整，而不是繼續糾纏。埃布羅河會戰中，共和軍以縱隊渡河，先頭步兵佔領灘頭後，裝甲旅在箭塔山一帶展開，逐次攻取陣地，最後把裝甲儲備集中於法容方向的總攻突擊；國民軍則以七十五與八十八毫米砲在反斜面集中射擊，並用馳援的M系列戰車嘗試攔截，但裝甲不足往往無法制止縱隊推進。空地配合上，國民軍依靠Ju 52/3m與He 111在晝間反覆轟炸共和軍縱隊與交通線，切斷其補給；共和軍空軍薄弱，早期縱隊推進只能靠夜行與晝夜交替，把損失壓到最低。補給方面，T-26行程短、油耗高、零件缺乏，維修多由戰地工兵拆解調配並從繳獲車上取件，大量車輛因行走裝置故障在行軍途中報廢，戰役後段的可用裝甲數因此急降。城市戰中坦克另有一套用法：狹窄街道限制射界，T-26多被停在交叉路口做固定射擊點，並利用敵方裝甲車必須逐棟轉向的弱點；步兵則用穿甲手榴彈與迫擊砲在近距離處理被擊中的裝甲車，時間拖得越久，防守方優勢越大。
tacticsEn: The core of Republican doctrine was to use the T-26 as mobile artillery rather than as a breakthrough weapon. Battalions were dispersed several hundred metres ahead of the infantry, companies leapfrogged once the attack went in, and when they met anti-tank fire they either halted in cover waiting for the infantry to suppress it or withdrew and let the infantry pass first. On the defensive they were echeloned in depth, tanks parked at street corners and building angles to serve as firing points, and against enemy armour they concentrated their guns on the front of the hull or on the tracks. When an attack failed the standard response was to break off and reform rather than to keep the engagement going. At the Ebro the Republican army crossed in columns, and once the leading infantry had seized the far shore the armoured brigades deployed around the Sierra de Pàndols, taking ground step by step before the armoured reserve was concentrated for the final offensive towards Fayón. The Nationalists answered with massed 75 and 88 mm fire from the reverse slopes and tried to counter-attack with hastily recalled M-series tanks, but their armour was too thin to stop the advancing columns. For air-ground cooperation the Nationalists used Ju 52/3m and He 111 bombers to strike Republican columns and lines of communication again and again in daylight, severing their supply; the Republican air force was too weak, and early columns could only move by night or in alternating day and night shifts to keep losses down. On the logistic side the T-26 had a short range, thirsty engines and a chronic shortage of spares, and repairs were improvised by field engineers cannibalising parts from wrecks; a great many vehicles were written off on the march through running gear failures, which is why the number of combat-ready tanks fell away so sharply in the later stages of every battle. Tank work in the cities followed its own rules: narrow streets restricted the arc of fire, so T-26s were usually parked at crossroads as fixed firing points, exploiting the weakness of enemy armour that had to turn corner by corner, while infantry disposed of immobilised vehicles with anti-tank grenades and mortars at close range, and the longer the delay the greater the advantage of the defenders. On the artillery side the Republic gradually learned to answer the Nationalists' massed fire with counter-battery work and echeloned shooting, raising fire control from regimental to army level.
data: 內戰自一九三六年七月十七日至一九三九年四月一日，前後約兩年八個半月。兵力方面，共和軍在一九三七年高峰時約四十萬人，國民軍同期約三十萬，其後因兼併地方部隊與外籍兵團補充而增至五十萬以上；國際縱隊總兵力約三萬五千至四萬五千人，分屬十九個縱隊。裝備方面，蘇聯自一九三六年十月起分批交付T-26：首批五十輛於十月抵達巴塞羅那，另有西班牙在一九三五年已訂購的五十輛在起義爆發前後到港，一九三七與一九三八年再交付數批，全部交付總數約二百五十輛上下；共和軍同時可用數通常在百輛上下，消耗最重的是布魯內特（1937年7月）與埃布羅河（1938年）兩役，單役損失常被估為數十輛。航空方面，義大利航空兵團在半島常駐飛機約六百架，德國康多爾空軍團最多時亦約六百架飛機、一萬九千名人員，整場戰爭執行數千架次出擊；共和國空軍靠蘇聯交付的數百架戰鬥機與轟炸機勉強支撐。埃布羅河會戰（一九三八年七月二十二日至十一月十六日）是全戰役規模最大的一役，雙方投入兵力合計逾五十萬，被普遍視為西班牙內戰中傷亡最慘重的會戰之一。全戰爭雙方作戰陣亡者合計達數十萬人。以上數字因史家統計口徑不同而略有出入，應視為概略範圍。裝甲交付的細節亦可核對：除T-26外，共和軍還有一批一九三五年購入的Vickers輕戰車同少量一戰時期英製FT-17，但數量遠不足以構成裝甲部隊，蘇聯顧問團本身亦曾評估把T-26改裝成步兵坦克的可行性。海上方面，英法封鎖線由一九三七年起逐步收緊，燃料與彈藥的進口量隨之大減。作戰節奏亦可對照：一九三六年下半年是城市與鄉村混合戰，一九三七年上半年共和軍在阿拉貢與埃斯特雷馬杜拉方向發動攻勢並一度逼近馬德里，同年下半年至一九三八年是國民軍的攻勢期，一九三八年七月之後雙方主力在埃布羅河反覆拉鋸至同年十一月。
dataEn: The civil war ran from 17 July 1936 to 1 April 1939, roughly two years and eight and a half months. On manpower, the Republican army peaked at about four hundred thousand men in 1937 while the Nationalists had around three hundred thousand at the same moment, growing beyond half a million later as local formations and foreign contingents were absorbed; the International Brigades numbered between thirty-five and forty-five thousand men spread over nineteen brigades. On equipment, the Soviet Union delivered T-26s in several shipments from October 1936: the first fifty reached Barcelona that month, the fifty ordered by Spain in 1935 arrived around the outbreak of the rising, and further batches followed in 1937 and 1938, for a total of roughly two hundred and fifty vehicles delivered. The number simultaneously available to the Republic usually hovered around a hundred, and the heaviest losses fell in Brunete in July 1937 and on the Ebro in 1938, with several dozen vehicles lost in a single action being the usual estimate. In the air, the Italian air force kept around six hundred aircraft on the peninsula and the Condor Legion at its height had some six hundred aircraft and nineteen thousand men, flying several thousand combat sorties over the whole war, while the Republican air force was barely kept alive by the Soviet delivery of several hundred fighters and bombers. The battle of the Ebro, from 22 July to 16 November 1938, was the largest action of the entire war, with more than half a million men committed between the two sides, and is widely regarded as the bloodiest engagement of the Spanish Civil War. Military deaths on both sides over the whole war ran into the hundreds of thousands. These figures vary a little between historians because the counting methods differ, and should be read as rough ranges. The detail of the deliveries can be checked: besides the T-26s the Republic held a batch of Vickers light tanks bought in 1935 and a few First World War British FT-17s, far too few to form an armoured force, and the Soviet advisers themselves studied the possibility of converting the T-26 into an infantry tank. At sea the blockade line drawn by Britain and France tightened through 1937, and imports of fuel and ammunition fell away with it. The rhythm of the fighting can be traced as well: the second half of 1936 was a mixture of urban and rural warfare; in the first half of 1937 the Republic launched offensives in Aragon and towards Extremadura and came close to Madrid; from the second half of 1937 through 1938 the Nationalists held the initiative, and after July 1938 the main forces of both sides fought up and down the Ebro until November of that year.
cause: 起義的直接背景，是第二共和國的改革把西班牙推向政治極化。一九三一年國王退位後成立的第二共和國，在一九三二至三四年推行土地改革、限制教會特權、裁減常備軍與推行世俗教育，這些措施同時觸動了大地主、教會與高級軍官。一九三六年二月人民陣線在選舉中取得大勝，使「共和」與「反共和」的對立徹底公開化；軍方一批軍官自一九三四年起便策劃推翻政府，一九三六年五月起由莫拉、卡瓦涅亞斯與桑胡爾霍等人在摩洛哥、薩拉戈薩與馬德里分別策劃，起義日期數度更改，最後定於七月十七日。七月十七日當天，起義在摩洛哥、薩拉戈薩與北部若干省成功，在馬德里與巴塞羅那等地卻因部隊倒向政府而失敗，叛軍在巴塞羅那幾乎全軍覆沒，於是本可逆轉的政變，變成雙方都不肯退讓的內戰。蘇聯與共產黨國際的援助、納粹德國與法西斯義大利的介入，以及法國等國發起卻無力執行的「不干預委員會」，使衝突在數月內升級為歐洲兩大陣營的代理人戰爭。外部條件同樣不可忽視：一九三五年義大利入侵埃塞俄比亞、納粹德國重新武裝並逐步退出凡爾賽體系，令西班牙的左右雙方都相信歐洲大戰遲早會到，於是各自搶先備戰。
causeEn: The immediate background to the rising was that the reforms of the Second Republic had pushed Spain into a state of political polarisation. After the king abdicated in 1931, the Republic that was established carried out land reform between 1932 and 1934, curtailed the privileges of the Church, cut the size of the standing army and pushed through secular education; the same measures antagonised the great landowners, the Church and the senior officer corps at once. The Popular Front's decisive victory at the elections of February 1936 made the confrontation between republican and anti-republican Spain completely open, and a group of army officers had been plotting the overthrow of the state since 1934. From May 1936 Mola, Cabanellas and Sanjurjo planned the rising separately in Morocco, Zaragoza and Madrid; the date was changed several times and finally fixed for 17 July. On that day the rising succeeded in Morocco, in Zaragoza and in several northern provinces, but in Madrid, Barcelona and elsewhere the troops stayed loyal to the government, and the insurgents were practically wiped out in Barcelona, so a coup that could still have been turned back turned into a civil war in which neither side would give way. Soviet and Comintern aid, the intervention of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, and the non-intervention committee set up by France and others without the means to enforce itself, raised the conflict within a few months into a proxy war between the two great camps of Europe. External conditions mattered too: the Italian invasion of Ethiopia in 1935, and the rearmament of Nazi Germany and its gradual withdrawal from the Versailles settlement, convinced both camps in Spain that a European war would come sooner rather than later, so each began to prepare in its own way.
impact: 這場內戰常被視為第二次世界大戰的預演，也成了新式戰爭的實驗場。康多爾空軍團在西班牙累積的俯衝轟炸、傘兵與工兵經驗，三年後直接在波蘭戰役與巴巴羅薩行動中重用；蘇聯則透過觀察T-26的表現反思裝甲理論，作為「西班牙步兵坦克」試驗的T-26系列車被大量生產，其車組骨幹成為日後蘇聯裝甲部隊的伏筆。義大利的志願兵軍團與航空兵團是法西斯國家第一次大規模海外用兵，德國也在干涉與不干預之間為自己找到位置。意識形態上，這是共產主義與法西斯主義第一次大規模直接對抗，數千名各國志願者組成國際縱隊參戰，在歐洲各國激發強烈的反獨裁同情，也催生一批作家與記者的戰地經歷。作戰方法上，城市防衛、裝甲砲兵與空地協同的經驗被各國觀察員帶回本土，國際縱隊人民陣線旅的編制與路線之爭，後來成為國際左翼運動的共同記憶。戰後，佛朗哥治下的「西班牙」在二戰中保持中立卻向軸心國提供鎢礦與兵員，使西班牙在大西洋兩岸成為關鍵節點，歐洲的和解也留下這道未竟裂縫；直到二〇一八年，西班牙才就「內戰與內戰後的暴行」立法追責，開始清算這段歷史。西班牙內戰亦改變了歐洲左翼的文學與影像：戰地記者拍下的空襲與街壘畫面，令整個歐洲的知識界第一次用影像理解現代化戰爭；康多爾空軍團的攝影團亦為德國空軍留下了宣傳與紀錄的經驗。
impactEn: The civil war is often treated as a rehearsal for the Second World War and as the proving ground for modern warfare. The lessons in dive bombing, parachute assault and combat engineering that the Condor Legion accumulated in Spain were reused three years later in the Polish campaign and in the opening of Operation Barbarossa; the Soviet Union, watching the T-26 in action, revised its own armoured doctrine, and the T-26 series built as the Spanish infantry tank experiment was put into large-scale production, the crews trained on it becoming the seed of Soviet armoured formations. The Italian Volunteer Corps and air force were the first large overseas deployment by a fascist state, and Germany found a position for itself between intervention and non-intervention. Ideologically this was the first large-scale direct clash between communism and fascism: several thousand volunteers from many countries fought in the International Brigades, stirring strong anti-fascist sympathy across Europe and giving a generation of writers and journalists their war experience. In operational terms, the experience of urban defence, armoured artillery and air-ground cooperation was carried home by foreign observers, and the debates over the organisation and the political line of the POUM within the International Brigades became a shared memory of the international left. After the war, Franco's Spain stayed nominally neutral in the Second World War while supplying the Axis with tungsten and troops, which made the country a strategic point on both shores of the Atlantic and left a rift that the reconciliation of Europe never quite closed; only in 2018 did Spain legislate on the civil war and the violence that followed it and begin to reckon with that history. The civil war also reshaped the literature and the imagery of the European left: pictures of air raids and street barricades taken by correspondents let the intellectual public of Europe understand a modern war through images for the first time, while the photographic units of the Condor Legion gave the German air force a body of experience in both publicity and record keeping.
result: 到一九三八年底，埃布羅河會戰的失敗加上英法對西班牙的武器封鎖，切斷了共和軍最後的彈藥與外援，國民軍於一九三九年二月攻佔加泰隆尼亞，數十萬共和國軍人與支持者越過庇里牛斯山撤入法國，另有船隊把人送往墨西哥與蘇聯。一九三九年三月，國民軍在全國各戰線發動總攻，並於三月二十七日在阿爾巴塞特附近的拉斯特塞斯與共和國參謀長卡薩多簽訂和約；三月廿八日國民軍進入馬德里，四月一日佛朗哥以廣播宣布戰爭結束，共和國政權在流亡中終止，簽署和約的卡薩多隨即被免職並遭拘禁。共和國軍被整編進國民軍序列，大批軍官遭解職，共產黨與人民陣線的組織遭到全面禁止。損失方面，內戰摧毀了西班牙大批工業、鐵路與農業設施，軍隊被解除武裝，國家的財政與外匯被耗盡，戰後的國際孤立更使佛朗哥治下的三十九年走向經濟停滯與警察體制。作為二戰的序幕，這場內戰換來的是歐洲的封鎖與冷淡；直到一九五〇年代西班牙才逐步回到國際社會，而那些參戰的縱隊老兵與流亡者，則把西班牙的教訓帶進了隨後的歐洲戰場。共和國的海軍與航空兵在戰敗時選擇南撤：艦隊經摩洛哥轉往法屬西非與加勒比基地，飛行員由法國港口飛抵摩洛哥再轉往蘇聯；大批檔案與設備隨撤退帶走，使戰後重建缺少可以立刻動用的資源。國民軍勝利之後，佛朗哥把共和國時期的軍用工業、煤礦與運輸重新編入國家計劃，對外貿易在戰後初期跌到谷底，國內同時實施嚴格的書籍與廣播審查。
resultEn: By the end of 1938 the defeat on the Ebro, together with the British and French arms blockade, cut off the Republic's last ammunition and foreign supply; in February 1939 the Nationalists took Catalonia, tens of thousands of Republican soldiers and supporters crossed the Pyrenees into France, and ships carried more of them to Mexico and to the Soviet Union. In March 1939 the Nationalists launched a general offensive on every front, and on 27 March the Republican chief of staff Casado signed the surrender at Yeste, near Albacete, with the emissaries of Franco; Nationalist troops entered Madrid on 28 March, and on 1 April Franco announced the end of the war by radio. The Republic ended in exile, and Casado, who had signed the surrender, was dismissed and arrested almost at once. The Republican army was incorporated into the Nationalist order of battle, large numbers of officers were removed, and the organisations of the communist party and the Popular Front were banned outright. As for losses, the war destroyed much of Spain's industrial, railway and agricultural base, the armed forces were disarmed, the national finances and foreign reserves were exhausted, and the international isolation that followed left the thirty-nine years of Franco's rule heading towards economic stagnation and a police state. As a prelude to the Second World War, the civil war bought Spain the blockade and the cold shoulder of Europe; the country only worked its way back into the international community in the 1950s, while the veterans of the brigades and the exiles carried the lessons of Spain into the European campaigns that followed. The Republican navy and air force chose to withdraw south as the front collapsed: the fleet went via Morocco to French West Africa and the Caribbean, and pilots flew from French ports to Morocco and onward to the Soviet Union, taking files and equipment with them, so that the postwar reconstruction lacked resources that could be put to work at once. After the Nationalist victory Franco folded the republican war economy, the coal mines and the railways back into the state plan, foreign trade fell to its lowest point in the early postwar years, and strict censorship of books and broadcasting was imposed at home.
